response.query: What are the top innovative trends in Health & Medical Sciences related to unsupervised MRI anomaly detection, including generative approaches, data privacy, clinical evaluation, and synthetic lesion validation?
response.answer: Top trends include generative adversarial networks for unsupervised MRI anomaly detection, variational autoencoders for reconstruction-based methods, and synthetic lesion validation for clinical evaluation. Privacy-preserving techniques are also being developed to protect patient data.

results.title: Towards Universal Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Medical Imaging
results.content: # Towards Universal Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Medical Imaging. The increasing complexity of medical imaging data underscores the need for advanced anomaly detection methods to automatically identify diverse pathologies. We evaluate the proposed method across various imaging modalities, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, pediatric wrist X-ray, and chest X-ray, and demonstrate superior performance in detecting anomalies compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. Our unsupervised anomaly detection approach may enhance diagnostic accuracy in medical imaging by identifying a broader range of unknown pathologies. Generative AI, Unsupervised Anomaly Detection, Medical Imaging. Historically, anomaly detection in medical imaging has relied heavily on supervised methods, designed to identify specific, well-defined pathologies like tumors (Menze et al., 2014), stroke (Liew et al., 2022), or white matter hyperintensities (Kuijf et al., 2019). However, a significant challenge in UAD has been its tendency to focus on evaluations using singular or a limited number of conditions, or employ self or weakly supervised methods (Wolleb et al., 2022; Kascenas et al., 2022) to estimate the ’unknown’ in anomaly detection. ## 2 Anomaly Detection in Medical Imaging. While this approach may demonstrate promising results for specific anomalies such as brain tumors, it is limited in its applicability to more general anomaly detection scenarios, as it relies on the distribution of the synthetic noise (Bercea et al., 2023c). Traditional Autoencoders (AEs) have been fundamental in establishing reconstruction-based methods for anomaly detection (Zimmerer et al., 2018). This adherence is crucial in medical imaging, where the precise characterization of normal anatomy is imperative for effective anomaly detection (Zimmerer et al., 2019). To advance the field of anomaly detection in medical imaging, we introduce the reversed AEs (RA). In this study, we introduced the Reversed Auto-Encoders (RA), an unsupervised anomaly detection framework, and conducted an extensive evaluation across various medical imaging modalities. Challenging Common Assumptions in Unsupervised Anomaly Detection, in: International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention, Springer. results.content: # Unsupervised Anomaly Detection with Generative Adversarial Networks to Guide Marker Discovery. AnoGAN, a deep convolutional generative adversarial network is proposed to learn a manifold of normal anatomical variability, accompanying a novel anomaly scoring scheme based on the mapping from image space to a latent space. The proposed generative adversarial network based on unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) based on minimum intensity projection (minIP) for the adversarial framework is a potential computer-aided tool for early detection of emphysema in lung cancer screening data. ### Unsupervised Deep Generative Models for Anomaly Detection in Neuroimaging: A Systematic Scoping Review. Looking ahead, unsupervised deep generative models offer a compelling direction for anomaly detection, enabling semi-supervised learning, supporting the discovery of novel imaging biomarkers, and facilitating within- and cross-disease deviation mapping in unified end-to-end frameworks. ### Unsupervised anomaly detection in brain FDG PET with deep generative models: An experimental analysis of model variability and mitigation strategies. This work proposes a novel approach that incorporates masking within diffusion models, leveraging their generative capabilities to learn robust representations of normal brain anatomy and surpasses existing unsupervised anomaly detection techniques, demonstrating superior performance in generating accurate normal counterparts and localizing anomalies. ### Simulation based evaluation framework for deep learning unsupervised anomaly detection on brain FDG-PET. A framework to evaluate unsupervised anomaly detection approaches that consists in simulating realistic anomalies from images of healthy subjects is proposed and demonstrated by evaluating an approach based on a 3D variational autoencoder. The identification of anomalies in large-scale medical imaging data is proposed using healthy examples as a reference and it is demonstrated that the learned features outperform standard embedding approaches in a classification task.

results.content: 6 Chapter 1 Introduction 2 Supervised- & Semi-supervised Deep Learning for Anomaly Detection in Brain MRI 2.1 Deﬁnition of Brain Anomaly Detection in a Supervised Context In their survey of traditional anomaly detection papers for medical image analysis, Taboada-Crispi et al.[94] differentiate between three different types of anomaly detection, based on degress of prior knowledge: a) methods completely devoid of prior knowledge, b) approaches which know alone about normality and c) techniques which utilize knowledge about both normal and abnormal cases. 3.2 Unsupervised Deep Representation Learning & Deep Generative Models In brain imaging, UAD has seen a wide array of methods, ranging from clustering-techniques based on unsupervised representation learning with AEs to the recent wave of distribution modeling with deep generative modeling frameworks such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and hybrids thereof.
